title: Functoriality of the maps on cohomology induced by f-maps
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_Y$-module, $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, $\varphi:\mathcal G\to h_*\mathcal F$ an $h$-map and $\varphi^*:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ ($p\ge0$) the map of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], with the cohomology groups of [pqf-def-cohomology]. (1) (Independence.) For a system of choices $C=(\mathcal I^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet,\mathcal J'^\bullet,\lambda,\beta)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], with $\mu=\Gamma(Y,\lambda)$, put $\varphi^*_C=(\iota^p_{\mathcal I})^{-1}\circ H^p(\mu)^{-1}\circ H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta))\circ\iota^p_{\mathcal J}$, where $\iota^p_{\mathcal I}:H^p(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ and $\iota^p_{\mathcal J}:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^\bullet))$ are the isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] for the global section functors $\Gamma(X,-)$ on $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\Gamma(Y,-)$ on $\mathcal O_Y$-modules (the identifications $H^p(X,\mathcal F)=H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$, $H^p(Y,\mathcal G)=H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^\bullet))$ of the definition). Then $\varphi^*_C=\varphi^*_{C'}$ for any two systems of choices $C$, $C'$. (2) (Composition.) Let $h:X\to Y$ and $k:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes, $\mathcal H$, $\mathcal G$, $\mathcal F$ modules on $Z$, $Y$, $X$, and $\psi:\mathcal H\to k_*\mathcal G$, $\varphi:\mathcal G\to h_*\mathcal F$ a $k$-map and an $h$-map. Then $k_*(\varphi)\circ\psi:\mathcal H\to k_*h_*\mathcal F=(k\circ h)_*\mathcal F$ is a $(k\circ h)$-map and $(k_*(\varphi)\circ\psi)^*=\varphi^*\circ\psi^*:H^p(Z,\mathcal H)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ for all $p\ge0$. In particular ($h$ or $k$ the identity) $\varphi^*\circ H^p(u)=(\varphi\circ u)^*$ and $H^p(v)\circ\varphi^*=(h_*(v)\circ\varphi)^*$ for morphisms of modules $u:\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G$ on $Y$ and $v:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ on $X$, $H^p(u)$, $H^p(v)$ the maps of the functors $H^p(Y,-)$, $H^p(X,-)$; and for the pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (a) along $k$, $h$, $k\circ h$, $(k\circ h)^*=H^p(c)\circ h^*\circ k^*:H^p(Z,\mathcal H)\to H^p(X,(k\circ h)^*\mathcal H)$, where $c:h^*k^*\mathcal H\to(k\circ h)^*\mathcal H$ is the canonical comparison morphism of pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback], i.e. the morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $(k\circ h)_*(c)\circ k_*(\eta^h_{k^*\mathcal H})\circ\eta^k_{\mathcal H}=\eta^{k\circ h}_{\mathcal H}$, $\eta^h,\eta^k,\eta^{k\circ h}$ the units of the adjunctions $h^*\dashv h_*$, $k^*\dashv k_*$, $(k\circ h)^*\dashv(k\circ h)_*$. (3) (Restriction.) Let $k:Y\to Z$, $\mathcal H$, $\mathcal G$, $\psi$ be as in (2), $V\subseteq Z$ open, $W=k^{-1}(V)$, $k|_W:W\to V$ the restricted morphism of open subschemes, and $\psi|_V:\mathcal H|_V\to(k|_W)_*(\mathcal G|_W)$ the morphism of $\mathcal O_V$-modules with components $\psi_T:\mathcal H(T)\to\mathcal G(k^{-1}T)$ for $T\subseteq V$ open (restricted modules as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]). Then $\mathrm{res}^Y_W\circ\psi^*=(\psi|_V)^*\circ\mathrm{res}^Z_V:H^p(Z,\mathcal H)\to H^p(W,\mathcal G|_W)$, with the restrictions of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b).

proof.text: *Lifts with the same degree-$0$ component give the same map.* Let $s_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ be an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] with $\mathcal J^n=0$ for $n<0$, $\mathcal J'^\bullet$ a complex of injective $\mathcal O_Y$-modules with $\mathcal J'^n=0$ for $n<0$, and $\beta_1,\beta_2:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ morphisms of complexes with $\beta_1^0\circ s_{\mathcal G}=\beta_2^0\circ s_{\mathcal G}$. The augmentation $\alpha:\mathcal G[0]\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ ($\alpha^0=s_{\mathcal G}$) is a quasi-isomorphism, as $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal J^0\to\mathcal J^1\to\cdots$ is exact, and $\beta_1\alpha=\beta_2\alpha$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy] $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$ are chain-homotopic, so by [lem-weil-pbc-homotopic-maps-equal-cohomology] applied to the additive functor $\Gamma(Y,-)$, $H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_1))=H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_2))$ for all $p$. The same holds on any scheme in place of $Y$; it is used below on $Y$ and on $Z$. (In particular, in a system of choices of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] any morphism of complexes $\beta$ with $\beta^0\circ s_{\mathcal G}=\lambda^0\circ h_*(s_{\mathcal F})\circ\varphi$ is admissible and all give the same $H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta))$.)

proof.text: *(1) for fixed $\mathcal I^\bullet$, $\mathcal J^\bullet$: independence of $(\mathcal J'^\bullet,\lambda,\beta)$.* Fix the injective resolutions $s_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$, $s_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal J^\bullet$. Since $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], [lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono] with $a=0$ gives a complex $\mathcal J'^\bullet_0$ of injective $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, zero in negative degrees, and a quasi-isomorphism $\lambda_0:h_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet_0$ which is a monomorphism in every degree; complete it by an admissible $\beta_0$ to a system $C_0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. Let $C_1=(\mathcal I^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet,\mathcal J'^\bullet_1,\lambda_1,\beta_1)$ be any system with the same $\mathcal I^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] ($K=h_*\mathcal I^\bullet$, $L=\mathcal J'^\bullet_0$, $\alpha=\lambda_0$, $\gamma=\lambda_1$; all bounded below) there is a morphism of complexes $c:\mathcal J'^\bullet_0\to\mathcal J'^\bullet_1$ with $c\lambda_0=\lambda_1$. Then $(c\beta_0)^0s_{\mathcal G}=c^0\lambda_0^0h_*(s_{\mathcal F})\varphi=\lambda_1^0h_*(s_{\mathcal F})\varphi$, so by Step 1 $H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_1))=H^p(\Gamma(Y,c))H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_0))$. Applying $\Gamma(Y,-)$ to $c\lambda_0=\lambda_1$ gives $H^p(\Gamma(Y,c))H^p(\mu_0)=H^p(\mu_1)$, where $\mu_i=\Gamma(Y,\lambda_i)$ are quasi-isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-module-pushforward-injectives-sections-quasi-iso]; hence $H^p(\mu_1)^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_1))=H^p(\mu_0)^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,c))^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,c))H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_0))=H^p(\mu_0)^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_0))$ ($H^p(\Gamma(Y,c))=H^p(\mu_1)H^p(\mu_0)^{-1}$ is invertible). So $\varphi^*_{C_1}=\varphi^*_{C_0}$: $\varphi^*_C$ depends only on $(\mathcal I^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet)$, and in computing it we may take $\lambda$ a monomorphism in every degree.

proof.text: *(1): independence of $\mathcal J^\bullet$.* Let $s_1:\mathcal G\to\mathcal J_1^\bullet$, $s_2:\mathcal G\to\mathcal J_2^\bullet$ be two injective resolutions (zero in negative degrees) and fix $\mathcal I^\bullet$, $\mathcal J'^\bullet$, $\lambda$. By [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists] (with $h=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G}$) there is a morphism of complexes $b:\mathcal J_1^\bullet\to\mathcal J_2^\bullet$ with $b^0s_1=s_2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] for $v=\Gamma(Y,-)$ (so $R^pv=H^p(Y,-)$ [pqf-def-cohomology]; $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]) and the morphism $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G}$, $\mathrm{id}=R^pv(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G})=(\iota^p_{\mathcal J_2})^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,b))\iota^p_{\mathcal J_1}$, i.e. $\iota^p_{\mathcal J_2}=H^p(\Gamma(Y,b))\iota^p_{\mathcal J_1}$. If $\beta_2$ is admissible for $\mathcal J_2^\bullet$, then $(\beta_2b)^0s_1=\beta_2^0s_2=\lambda^0h_*(s_{\mathcal F})\varphi$, so $\beta_2b$ is admissible for $\mathcal J_1^\bullet$ (Step 1), and $(\iota^p_{\mathcal I})^{-1}H^p(\mu)^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_2b))\iota^p_{\mathcal J_1}=(\iota^p_{\mathcal I})^{-1}H^p(\mu)^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_2))\iota^p_{\mathcal J_2}$. With Step 2, $\varphi^*_C$ depends only on $\mathcal I^\bullet$.

proof.text: *(1): independence of $\mathcal I^\bullet$; end of (1).* Let $s_1:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I_1^\bullet$, $s_2:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I_2^\bullet$ be two injective resolutions (zero in negative degrees) and fix $\mathcal J^\bullet$. By [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists] there is $a:\mathcal I_1^\bullet\to\mathcal I_2^\bullet$ with $a^0s_1=s_2$, and as in Step 3 ([lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] for $\Gamma(X,-)$ and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F}$) $\iota^p_{\mathcal I_2}=H^p(\Gamma(X,a))\iota^p_{\mathcal I_1}$, so $H^p(\Gamma(X,a))$ is invertible. Take any system $C_2=(\mathcal I_2^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet,\mathcal J'^\bullet_2,\lambda_2,\beta_2)$ and, by Step 2, a system $C_1=(\mathcal I_1^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet,\mathcal J'^\bullet_1,\lambda_1,\beta_1)$ with $\lambda_1$ a monomorphism in every degree. $h_*(a):h_*\mathcal I_1^\bullet\to h_*\mathcal I_2^\bullet$ is a morphism of complexes ($h_*$ is a functor [def-pc-module-pullback]); by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] ($\alpha=\lambda_1$, $\gamma=\lambda_2h_*(a)$) there is $c:\mathcal J'^\bullet_1\to\mathcal J'^\bullet_2$ with $c\lambda_1=\lambda_2h_*(a)$. Then $(c\beta_1)^0s_{\mathcal G}=c^0\lambda_1^0h_*(s_1)\varphi=\lambda_2^0h_*(a^0s_1)\varphi=\lambda_2^0h_*(s_2)\varphi$, so $c\beta_1$ is admissible for $C_2$ and by Step 1 $H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_2))=H^p(\Gamma(Y,c))H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_1))$. Since $\Gamma(Y,h_*(a))=\Gamma(X,a)$ (definition of $h_*$), $\Gamma(Y,-)$ applied to $c\lambda_1=\lambda_2h_*(a)$ gives $H^p(\Gamma(Y,c))H^p(\mu_1)=H^p(\mu_2)H^p(\Gamma(X,a))$, with $\mu_1,\mu_2$ quasi-isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-module-pushforward-injectives-sections-quasi-iso]; so $H^p(\mu_2)^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,c))=H^p(\Gamma(X,a))H^p(\mu_1)^{-1}$ and $\varphi^*_{C_2}=(\iota^p_{\mathcal I_2})^{-1}H^p(\mu_2)^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,c))H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_1))\iota^p_{\mathcal J}=(\iota^p_{\mathcal I_1})^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(X,a))^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(X,a))H^p(\mu_1)^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta_1))\iota^p_{\mathcal J}=\varphi^*_{C_1}$. Together with Steps 2 and 3 (which make $\varphi^*_C$ a function of $\mathcal I^\bullet$ alone), $\varphi^*_C=\varphi^*_{C'}$ for any two systems: this is (1).

proof.text: *(2): the composite is a $(k\circ h)$-map.* For an open $T\subseteq Z$, $(k_*h_*\mathcal F)(T)=(h_*\mathcal F)(k^{-1}T)=\mathcal F(h^{-1}k^{-1}T)=\mathcal F((k\circ h)^{-1}T)=((k\circ h)_*\mathcal F)(T)$ with the same restriction maps, and the $\mathcal O_Z(T)$-module structures agree because $(k\circ h)^\sharp_T=h^\sharp_{k^{-1}T}\circ k^\sharp_T$ (composition of morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]); so $k_*h_*\mathcal F=(k\circ h)_*\mathcal F$, likewise $k_*h_*=(k\circ h)_*$ on morphisms and complexes. $k_*(\varphi)$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_Z$-modules ($k_*$ is a functor $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-pc-module-pullback]), hence so is $k_*(\varphi)\circ\psi:\mathcal H\to(k\circ h)_*\mathcal F$.

proof.text: *(2): the special cases.* (i) For $u:\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G$ on $Y$ apply (2) with $(Z,Y,X)=(Y,Y,X)$, $k=\mathrm{id}_Y$, $\psi=u$ (an $\mathrm{id}_Y$-map, $(\mathrm{id}_Y)_*\mathcal G=\mathcal G$): $(\varphi\circ u)^*=\varphi^*\circ u^*$, and $u^*=H^p(u)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-basic-properties] (3). (ii) For $v:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ on $X$ apply (2) with $(Z,Y,X)=(Y,X,X)$, $k=h$, $\psi=\varphi$, and the $\mathrm{id}_X$-map $v$: $(h_*(v)\circ\varphi)^*=v^*\circ\varphi^*=H^p(v)\circ\varphi^*$ by the same clause (3). (iii) Pullbacks. The maps $f\mapsto h_*(f)\circ\eta^h_{k^*\mathcal H}$, $\mathrm{Hom}(h^*k^*\mathcal H,M)\to\mathrm{Hom}(k^*\mathcal H,h_*M)$, and $g\mapsto k_*(g)\circ\eta^k_{\mathcal H}$, $\mathrm{Hom}(k^*\mathcal H,N)\to\mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal H,k_*N)$, are the adjunction bijections [def-pc-module-pullback]; their composite is $f\mapsto(k\circ h)_*(f)\circ k_*(\eta^h_{k^*\mathcal H})\circ\eta^k_{\mathcal H}$ (Step 5), so $c$ exists and is unique. By (2) applied to $\psi=\eta^k_{\mathcal H}$ and $\varphi=\eta^h_{k^*\mathcal H}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (a), $h^*\circ k^*=(k_*(\eta^h_{k^*\mathcal H})\circ\eta^k_{\mathcal H})^*$; by (ii) with $v=c$, $H^p(c)\circ h^*\circ k^*=((k\circ h)_*(c)\circ k_*(\eta^h_{k^*\mathcal H})\circ\eta^k_{\mathcal H})^*=(\eta^{k\circ h}_{\mathcal H})^*=(k\circ h)^*$.

proof.text: *(3).* Let $j_V:V\to Z$, $j_W:W\to Y$ be the inclusions; $k\circ j_W=j_V\circ k|_W:W\to Z$. $\psi|_V$ is well defined: for $T\subseteq V$ open, $((k|_W)_*(\mathcal G|_W))(T)=\mathcal G(k^{-1}T\cap W)=\mathcal G(k^{-1}T)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], and the $\psi_T$ are $\mathcal O_Z(T)$-linear and compatible with restriction. By [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b), $\mathrm{res}^Y_W=\rho_{\mathcal G}^*$ and $\mathrm{res}^Z_V=\rho_{\mathcal H}^*$ for the restriction maps $\rho_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to j_{W*}(\mathcal G|_W)$, $\rho_{\mathcal H}:\mathcal H\to j_{V*}(\mathcal H|_V)$. By (2), $\mathrm{res}^Y_W\circ\psi^*=(k_*(\rho_{\mathcal G})\circ\psi)^*$ and $(\psi|_V)^*\circ\mathrm{res}^Z_V=(j_{V*}(\psi|_V)\circ\rho_{\mathcal H})^*$, both maps of $(k\circ j_W)$-maps $\mathcal H\to(k\circ j_W)_*(\mathcal G|_W)$, whose module of sections over $T\subseteq Z$ open is $\mathcal G(k^{-1}T\cap W)$. On $t\in\mathcal H(T)$ the first sends $t$ to $\psi_T(t)|_{k^{-1}T\cap W}$, the second to $\psi_{T\cap V}(t|_{T\cap V})\in\mathcal G(k^{-1}(T\cap V))=\mathcal G(k^{-1}T\cap W)$; these agree because $\psi$ commutes with the restriction from $T$ to $T\cap V$. So the two $(k\circ j_W)$-maps are equal, and so are their maps on $H^p$.
